Long ago, the sky was a blanket of velvet charcoal, devoid of color. The Sun, a golden king, slept soundly, and his sister, the Moon, was too shy to reveal her face. The mortals below shivered in the eternal, icy gloom. Among them lived a weaver named Elara, who possessed a loom carved from starlight. She spent her nights gathering the flickers of distant constellations, threading them onto a spindle of frozen mist.

One midwinter eve, as the cold threatened to extinguish the last fires of the village, Elara climbed the highest peak. She threw her luminous tapestry into the biting wind. The threads, charged with the dreams of the sleeping world, unfurled across the heavens. They danced, weaving emerald ribbons and violet veils through the dark canopy. The stars shivered in delight, and the world was bathed in a spectral, shifting glow. The Sun woke, marveling at his sister’s new gown of radiance. Since that night, whenever the world grows too cold or the shadows stretch too long, the Great Weaver tosses her shimmering threads into the sky, reminding us that even in the deepest winter, there is beauty waiting to be found in the dark.
